united-states-renewable-fuel-standard-fe.name: United States - Renewable Fuel Standard (federal)
united-states-renewable-fuel-standard-fe.fuels: Ethanol, biodiesel / renewable diesel, cellulosic, advanced biofuels
united-states-renewable-fuel-standard-fe.policy: Federal mandate: refiners and importers must blend set annual volumes of renewable fuel into transport fuel, tracked with tradable RINs. EPA sets annual Renewable Volume Obligations (RVOs).
united-states-renewable-fuel-standard-fe.implemented: 2005 (Energy Policy Act)†; expanded as RFS2 in 2007 (Energy Independence and Security Act)†.
changes: 2025 - Total RVO of 22.61 bn gallons (baseline for the later increase). EPA was late setting 2026 volumes (statutory deadline was Nov 2024).
Jun 2025 - EPA proposed 2026-27 volumes ('Set 2'), including a proposal to halve RINs for imported biofuel and imported feedstocks.
Sep 2025 - EPA reallocation framework for small refinery exemptions (SREs); 50% or 100% reallocation considered.
27 Mar 2026 - Final Set 2 rule announced; published in the Federal Register 1 Apr 2026.
united-states-renewable-fuel-standard-fe.latest: Set 2 final rule (effective 15 Jun 2026): total renewable fuel 25.82 bn RINs (2026) and 25.98 bn RINs (2027); advanced biofuel 10.82 / 10.98 bn RINs; implied conventional (corn ethanol) volume held at 15 bn gal in both years; biomass-based diesel now expressed in RINs instead of gallons; 70% reallocation of waived 2023-25 SREs; partial waiver of the 2025 cellulosic volume (170 mn RIN shortfall); eRIN pathways eliminated. Percentage standards 2026: total 15.50%, advanced 6.42%, biomass-based diesel 5.24%; 2027: 15.78%, 6.61%, 5.37%.
united-states-renewable-fuel-standard-fe.pending: Half-RIN treatment for imported biofuel/feedstock was dropped from the final rule, but EPA says it intends to pursue it in the next rule ('Set 3', 2028 onward).

united-states-tax-credits-45z-and-e15-ru.name: United States - Tax credits (45Z) and E15 rules (federal)
united-states-tax-credits-45z-and-e15-ru.policy: 45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit (technology-neutral, based on carbon intensity) plus Clean Air Act treatment of E15 (15% ethanol) summer sales.
united-states-tax-credits-45z-and-e15-ru.implemented: 45Z: created by the Inflation Reduction Act (2022), operative from 2025†. E15: EPA emergency summer waivers issued every year since 2022.
changes: 4 Jul 2025 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act extended 45Z by two years through end-2029, limited eligible feedstocks to the US, Canada and Mexico, and kept full transferability.
2025 - EPA approved year-round E15 for eight Midwest states (IL, IA, MN, MO, NE, OH, SD, WI) at their governors' request; SD and OH were pending until 2026.
Feb 2026 - Treasury released proposed 45Z regulations; public hearing scheduled for 28 May 2026.
13 May 2026 - House passed the Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act (year-round E15 nationwide).
united-states-tax-credits-45z-and-e15-ru.latest: 45Z is in force through 2029 under the 2025 tax law, operating under proposed (not final) Treasury rules; USDA feedstock guidance described as imminent (Jun 2026). Year-round E15 is available in the approved Midwest states; nationwide year-round E15 is not yet law.
united-states-tax-credits-45z-and-e15-ru.pending: Senate vote on year-round E15 (as of Jun 2026); final 45Z regulations and USDA feedstock guidance; Biodiesel Tax Credit Extension Act of 2026 (introduced Apr 2026).
united-states-tax-credits-45z-and-e15-ru.flags: Status after Jun 2026 not confirmed in sources found.

united-states-california-low-carbon-fuel.name: United States - California Low Carbon Fuel Standard
united-states-california-low-carbon-fuel.fuels: Ethanol, biodiesel, renewable diesel, biogas, other low-carbon fuels
united-states-california-low-carbon-fuel.policy: Market-based standard requiring a declining carbon intensity (CI) of California transport fuels; deficits and credits are traded.
united-states-california-low-carbon-fuel.implemented: 2011 (program in operation since 2011); original goal: 10% CI cut from a 2010 baseline by 2020.
changes: 8 Nov 2024 - CARB board approved amendments.
Feb 2025 - Office of Administrative Law (OAL) disapproved the first submission; CARB resubmitted 16 May 2025.
27 Jun 2025 - OAL approved; amended rule effective 1 Jul 2025.
united-states-california-low-carbon-fuel.latest: Amended LCFS (effective 1 Jul 2025): CI reduction of 30% by 2030 and 90% by 2045 versus 2010; one-time 9% step-down in 2025 (22.75% reduction); new auto-adjustment mechanism; limits on crop-based biofuel participation.
united-states-california-low-carbon-fuel.pending: Legal challenges and fuel-price debate continuing (mid-2025 law-firm commentary).
united-states-california-low-carbon-fuel.flags: Two different CI standards applied within calendar year 2025 (before and after 1 Jul).

canada.name: Canada
canada.policy: Federal Clean Fuel Regulations (CFR): suppliers must cut the life-cycle carbon intensity of gasoline and diesel, with a credit market; the CFR also carries minimum renewable content of 5% in gasoline and 2% in diesel. Provincial mandates and a federal Biofuels Production Incentive add to this.
canada.implemented: CFR took effect 1 Jul 2023 (SOR/2022-140). Earlier federal Renewable Fuel Regulations set the 5% / 2% minimums†. Clean Fuels Fund of C$1.5 bn announced in Budget 2021.
changes: 1 Apr 2025 - British Columbia: diesel renewable content raised from 4% to 8% and must be Canadian-produced.
7 Aug 2025 - Ontario Reg. 663/20 amended: at least 75% of required diesel renewable content (2026 onward) and 64% of gasoline renewable content (2026-27) must be produced in Canada.
5 Sep 2025 - Federal government announced a Biofuels Production Incentive (over C$370 mn) and intent to amend the CFR.
3 Dec 2025 - Discussion paper on targeted CFR amendments (updated 19 Dec 2025).
1 Jan 2026 - BC gasoline 5% renewable content must be Canadian-made; Biofuels Production Incentive launched 5 Jan 2026.
canada.latest: CFR in force. Biofuels Production Incentive (over C$372 mn; per-litre support for biodiesel and renewable diesel, Jan 2026 - Dec 2027) in effect. Domestic-content rules in BC and Ontario. 2025 data: ethanol about 10% of the gasoline pool; biomass-based diesel over 7% nationally.
canada.pending: Draft targeted CFR amendments (not found finalized); formal CFR review to begin in 2027.

brazil.name: Brazil
brazil.policy: Layered system: mandatory ethanol blend in gasoline; mandatory biodiesel blend in diesel (PNPB); RenovaBio (Law 13,576/2017, decarbonization credits); Fuel of the Future Law (Law 14,993/2024) setting blend ceilings plus SAF and biomethane programs. Blend changes require approval by the CNPE energy council.
brazil.implemented: Ethanol blending since the 1970s (Proalcool)†; mandatory biodiesel blending since 2005; RenovaBio 2017; Fuel of the Future Law signed 8-9 Oct 2024.
changes: 2015 - Gasoline ethanol blend set at E27.
Apr 2023 - Biodiesel B12; Mar 2024 - B14.
Oct 2024 - Fuel of the Future Law: ethanol up to E35 and biodiesel up by 1 point each March to B20 by 2030 (subject to CNPE approval); SAF use from 2027.
1 Aug 2025 - Ethanol E27 to E30 and biodiesel B14 to B15 (CNPE announced 25 Jun 2025).
Mar 2026 - Scheduled B16 step; as of Jul 2026 reporting B15 was still in force (feasibility tests unfinished).
14 Jul 2026 - CNPE approved new biodiesel rules (ban on imported biodiesel for meeting the mandate; room for voluntary higher blends) and a temporary increase of the gasoline ethanol blend to 32%.
brazil.latest: E30 (since Aug 2025) with a CNPE-approved temporary increase to E32 (14 Jul 2026; trade press of 20 Oct 2026 reports Brazil hiking ethanol blending to 32%). B15 biodiesel mandate with a ban on imported biodiesel for compliance. SAF mandate scheduled from 2027.
brazil.pending: Studies on E35 and other higher blends; statutory path to B20 by 2030; B16 step.
brazil.flags: Effective date of E32 not confirmed in sources found. Some republished articles carry 2026 dates for 2025 events.

argentina.name: Argentina
argentina.policy: Law 27,640 (Biofuels Regulatory Framework): mandatory blends of bioethanol in gasoline and biodiesel in diesel, using domestically produced feedstock. No direct financial support.
argentina.implemented: Earlier biofuels law 26,093 (2006)†; Law 27,640 passed Jul 2021 and valid to 2030.
changes: 2021 - Law 27,640: ethanol 12% (6% sugarcane, 6% corn); biodiesel cut by five points to 5%.
Jun 2022 - Biodiesel blend raised from 5% to 7.5%.
Mar 2026 - Regulation lets distributors blend up to 15% ethanol voluntarily above the 12% mandate.
argentina.latest: 12% ethanol / 7.5% biodiesel mandate in force through 2030 (Law 27,640); voluntary ethanol blending up to 15% allowed since Mar 2026.
argentina.pending: Reform bill: ethanol 12% to 15% and biodiesel 7.5% to 10%, taking full effect 12 months after enactment; a single producer would be capped at 20% of ethanol volume. Some reports say the Senate approved it, but Aug-Sep 2026 coverage shows lawmakers weighing splitting biodiesel from the bill and industry still urging passage.
argentina.flags: Final enactment status unclear in sources found - verify.

paraguay.name: Paraguay
paraguay.policy: Mandatory ethanol blend in gasoline and a biodiesel blend regime administered by the Ministry of Industry and Commerce (MIC).
paraguay.implemented: Ethanol mandate historically E24-E25 (older sources); E30 minimum set Mar 2025.
changes: Mar 2025 - Became the first country to mandate a minimum 30% ethanol blend (E30).
5-7 May 2026 - One report says the president signed a law raising the minimum sugarcane ethanol blend to 50%; another describes a requirement that 50% of the ethanol blended be domestic feedstock.
23 Jun 2026 - MIC set the biodiesel blend band at 8-10% within a new legal range of 5-20%.
About 20 Jul 2026 - 8% biodiesel mandate entered into force; on 24 Jul 2026 MIC cut it back to 7% for 24 Jul - 31 Dec 2026 (compliance checks start after 60 days).
paraguay.latest: Ethanol: E30 minimum (Mar 2025) plus the May 2026 law (see flag). Biodiesel: 7% through 31 Dec 2026.
paraguay.pending: Operating band within the 5-20% legal range for 2027 onward.
paraguay.flags: Conflicting reports on what the May 2026 ethanol law requires (50% blend vs 50% domestic content) - verify against the official gazette.

colombia.name: Colombia
colombia.policy: National ethanol (E10) and biodiesel (B10) blend mandates; domestic palm oil supplies biodiesel.
colombia.implemented: Ethanol mandate since 2005 (applied unevenly; E8-E10 in most of the country since mid-2017).
changes: May 2021 - Ethanol mandate temporarily cut from E10 to E4 (weather-hit production, high US ethanol prices).
Aug 2025 - Ecopetrol introduced a marine fuel blend (small additional biodiesel demand).
2026 - Target of 1% SAF (about 27 mn liters) and CORSIA-aligned procedures.
colombia.latest: B10 unchanged in 2026 (USDA); E10 in major cities. Biodiesel production forecast up 4.5% to 765 mn liters in 2026.
colombia.flags: One aggregator roundup reports B12 to B13 in Jul 2024, which conflicts with USDA's B10; USDA figure used here.

other-latin-america-snapshot.name: Other Latin America (snapshot)
other-latin-america-snapshot.policy: National ethanol blend mandates per US Grains Council map: Bolivia E25; Peru E7.8; Costa Rica E10 (2025); Guatemala E10 (2026); Panama E10 (by 2026); Jamaica E10; Uruguay E10. Mexico: blending applies outside Mexico City, Monterrey and Guadalajara (details truncated in source).
changes: Not researched country by country.
other-latin-america-snapshot.latest: Levels as listed in the Apr 2025 US Grains Council blending map.
other-latin-america-snapshot.flags: Single industry source (Apr 2025 snapshot); implementation status and dates vary and were not verified.

european-union-red-iii.name: European Union (RED III)
european-union-red-iii.policy: Renewable Energy Directive: binding renewable-energy and transport targets that member states turn into national fuel-supplier obligations.
european-union-red-iii.implemented: RED I 2009 (10% renewables in transport by 2020)†; RED II 2018†; RED III (Directive (EU) 2023/2413) adopted 18 Oct 2023 and in force 20 Nov 2023.
changes: Nov 2023 - RED III lifted the EU renewables target from 32% to at least 42.5% by 2030 (indicative 45%).

Transport: member states choose either at least 29% renewables in transport by 2030 or a 14.5% GHG-intensity cut by 2030; combined binding sub-target for advanced biofuels/biogas and RFNBOs of 1% in 2025 and 5.5% in 2030.
May 2025 - Transposition deadline: only two member states had transposed (at least the transport part) on time.
Jan 2026 - European Biodiesel Board launched a RED III transposition tracker; several, not all, states done; some final texts not expected until 2027.
european-union-red-iii.latest: RED III in force; national transposition uneven (see Germany, France, Ireland, Spain, Netherlands). USDA's 2026 EU Biofuels Annual (Aug 2026): bioethanol production stagnant in 2026; biomass-based diesel output forecast up 4.2%.
european-union-red-iii.pending: Remaining member-state transposition; further national decisions on obligations beyond 2030.

germany.name: Germany
germany.policy: Greenhouse Gas Reduction Quota (THG-Quote): fuel suppliers must cut the GHG intensity of fuels, with tradable certificates; the main route for biofuels.
changes: Before reform - Quota ran only to 2030 (25.1% in 2030).
Jun and Oct 2025 - Ministerial drafts of the RED III bill.

10 Dec 2025 - Cabinet approved the Second Law on the GHG Quota: 12% (2026), 25% (2030), 36% (2035), 59% (2040); double counting of advanced biofuels ends from the 2026 compliance year (except fuel placed on the market before 1 Jan 2026); palm oil products incl. POME excluded (from 2027 per one source); advanced-biofuel sub-quota 2.0% (2026), 3.5% (2030), 9% (2040); RFNBO sub-quota 0.1% (2026) rising to 8% (2040); SAF mandate; shipping left out.
germany.latest: A 2026 industry commentary states Germany has implemented RED III for transport and finalized the quota reform, extending the obligation to 2040.
germany.flags: That commentary cites a 65% GHG reduction by 2040, versus 59% in the cabinet draft - verify the enacted figure in the Federal Law Gazette.

france.name: France
france.policy: TIRUERT: an incentive tax on fuel suppliers that falls away when renewable-energy incorporation targets are met (no direct blending mandate).
france.implemented: In place for years under earlier names (TGAP / TIRIB)†; legal basis article 266 quindecies of the customs code, now article 300 bis of the tax code.
changes: Plan - RED III would replace TIRUERT with a new mechanism (IRICC) from 1 Jan 2026.
Late 2025 / early 2026 - IRICC delayed to 1 Jan 2027; TIRUERT extended through 31 Dec 2026.
2026 - TIRUERT target percentages kept at 2025 levels.
30 Jul 2026 - Decree 2026-703 adds eligible hydrogen; new traceability rules apply from 1 Aug 2026.
france.latest: TIRUERT in force through 31 Dec 2026 at 2025 target levels.
france.pending: IRICC from 1 Jan 2027. Consultation proposals (not law): diesel 9% (2026), 11.4% (2030), 16% (2035); gasoline 9.5%, 10.5%, 14.5%; crop cap 7%; penalty EUR 700/t CO2e. Final adoption of the enabling bill before 31 Dec 2026 described as uncertain.
france.flags: Consultation figures are proposals, not enacted rules.

ireland.name: Ireland
ireland.policy: Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation (RTFO) transposing the RED III transport rules.
ireland.implemented: Regulations effective 1 Jan 2026 for the current rates (earlier obligation scheme not researched).
changes: Dec 2025 - Transport Minister signed regulations setting 2026 rates.
1 Jan 2026 - RTFO rate 32%; advanced biofuel + RFNBO obligation 5%; crop cap 3%. The rate is lower than first anticipated but above 2025. Advanced obligation widened to include RFNBOs.
ireland.latest: RTFO 32%, advanced + RFNBO 5%, crop cap 3% (from 1 Jan 2026).
ireland.flags: Basis of the 32% figure (energy vs GHG) not stated in the sources - check the regulations.

spain.name: Spain
spain.policy: Proposed Royal Decree transposing the RED III transport rules.
spain.implemented: Not yet enacted (draft as of Feb 2026).
changes: Feb 2026 - Draft Royal Decree welcomed by transport and energy sectors: overall transport emissions-reduction target plus a sub-target of at least 18.5% renewable energy in road transport by 2040; 1.7% limit on contribution from Annex IX Part B feedstocks.
2026 - Industry (e.g. APPA Biocarburantes) objected to letting RFNBOs used outside transport count toward transport targets.
spain.latest: No enacted RED III transport decree found.

netherlands.name: Netherlands
netherlands.policy: Energy for Transport regulation: moving from energy-based obligations to a GHG-savings mechanism under RED III.
changes: Sep 2025 - Updated draft amendment published for consultation: confirms end of double counting for Annex IX feedstock; stricter verification and documentation.
29 Sep 2025 - Ministry meeting on RED III implementation; study on extending obligations beyond 2030 due Nov 2025, decisions expected early 2026.
netherlands.latest: Not confirmed as enacted in sources found.

united-kingdom-renewable-transport-fuel-.name: United Kingdom - Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation
united-kingdom-renewable-transport-fuel-.policy: RTFO: suppliers must supply a rising share of renewable transport fuel, with a development-fuel sub-target and a crop cap.
changes: 15 Apr 2018 - Targets raised: main obligation at least 12.4% by 2032; first support for renewable aviation fuels.
2021-22 - 'Targeting net zero' response: main obligation raised (from 9.6%) to 14.6% by 2032; development fuel target 2.8% by 2032; recycled carbon fuels supported.
15 Aug 2025 - DfT published outcome of the statutory review (128 responses): proposals on future target trajectory, development fuels and broadening to nuclear-derived fuels.
2026 - DfT reduced the publication frequency of RTFO statistics.
united-kingdom-renewable-transport-fuel-.latest: Main obligation rising to 14.6% by 2032, then flat; development fuel obligation 2.8% by 2032. No change to targets found enacted since the review.
united-kingdom-renewable-transport-fuel-.pending: Further consultation on post-2032 trajectory, including options for higher targets.

uk-and-eu-saf-mandates-aviation.name: UK and EU - SAF mandates (aviation)
uk-and-eu-saf-mandates-aviation.policy: Binding SAF blending obligations on jet fuel suppliers: UK SAF Mandate and EU ReFuelEU Aviation.
uk-and-eu-saf-mandates-aviation.implemented: Both applied from 2025 (UK mandate in force 1 Jan 2025).
changes: Nov 2024 - UK Parliament approved the SAF Mandate.
UK schedule: 2% (2025), 10% (2030), 15% (2035), 22% (2040), flat thereafter; HEFA pathway capped at 100% (2025-26), 71% (2030), 35% (2040); power-to-liquid sub-mandate from 2028.
uk-and-eu-saf-mandates-aviation.latest: Both mandates in force at 2% for 2025, rising on the schedules shown.
uk-and-eu-saf-mandates-aviation.pending: UK Revenue Certainty Mechanism for SAF producers (legislation announced Jul 2024).

india.name: India
india.policy: Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme and the National Policy on Biofuels 2018 (amended 2022): blending targets, broader feedstock (cane juice, grains, damaged grain with committee approval), incentives for advanced biofuels, and a 5% biodiesel target.
india.implemented: EBP launched 2003†; National Policy on Biofuels announced May 2018.
changes: 2018 - Policy set 20% ethanol and 5% biodiesel blending by 2030.
Jun 2022 - Amendment advanced the E20 target to ethanol supply year (ESY) 2025-26.
2013-14 to 2024-25 - Average blending rose from about 1.5% to 19.2%.
Nov 2025 - Jun 2026 - Average 20% blend achieved in ESY 2025-26, five years ahead of the original 2030 target.
1 Apr 2026 - Centre mandated nationwide sale of petrol with up to 20% ethanol and minimum RON 95.
india.latest: E20 is the nationwide standard from 1 Apr 2026. Government said (Jul 2026) no decision has been taken to raise the base blend beyond E20.
india.pending: E30 preparation (BIS standard IS 19850:2026; transition expected 2028-30); draft SAF policy being finalized; informal SAF targets 1% (2027), 2% (2028), 5% (2030) for international flights (non-binding).

indonesia.name: Indonesia
indonesia.policy: Mandatory palm-based biodiesel blending in diesel, financed by a palm oil export levy; a small ethanol allowance (E3).
indonesia.implemented: Mandatory biodiesel since 2008†; B35 in 2023; B40 from 1 Jan 2025.
changes: 1 Jan 2025 - B40 mandate took effect (highest blend in the world).
Dec 2025 - 2026 biodiesel quota set at 15.646 mn kl (B40 basis).
Jan 2026 - Government confirmed B40 for 2026 and delayed B50 (financing concerns).
30 Mar 2026 - President announced B50 for 2026.
8 Apr 2026 - Ministerial decree on the blending timeline (a Malaysian Palm Oil Board digest headline says all users move to B50 by 2028).
25 Jun 2026 - Regulation issued to implement B50 from 1 Jul 2026 with a three-month transition for retailers.
indonesia.latest: B50 mandate from 1 Jul 2026 (B40 in Jan-Jun 2026), with a three-month retailer transition. A new allocation decree for H2 2026 was still to be issued (B40 allocation was 15.65 mn kl; B50 demand projected at 17.6 mn kl).
indonesia.pending: SAF mandate planned from 2027 (1% in 2027, 2.5% by 2030); H2 2026 biodiesel allocation decree.
indonesia.flags: Latest retrieved reports (Jun-Jul 2026) describe preparation and launch; no post-July implementation report was retrieved - check current status.

malaysia.name: Malaysia
malaysia.policy: National Biodiesel Programme: palm methyl ester blend mandates for diesel.
changes: 2019 - B10 for the transport sector.
Feb 2020 - B20 programme in Labuan, Langkawi and Sarawak (excluding Bintulu); nationwide B20 has stalled.
14 Apr 2026 - Government announced B10 to B15, starting with B12.
1 Jun 2026 - B15 rollout across Peninsular Malaysia.
malaysia.latest: B15 from 1 Jun 2026 (Peninsular Malaysia); B20 in selected regions.
malaysia.pending: B30 mandate for commercial and public transport; B20/B30 depot upgrades under the 13th Malaysia Plan (2026-30); nationwide B30 by 2030 target; SAF 1% by 2027.
malaysia.flags: A 30 Jul 2026 article still describes B15 as planned (appears to be a republished April item).

thailand.name: Thailand
thailand.policy: Gasohol and biodiesel programs supported by retail price differentials, excise tax and oil-fund subsidies; diesel grades B7 and B20.
thailand.implemented: Gasohol and biodiesel promotion since the early 2000s†.
changes: 1 May 2024 - B10 sales discontinued; only B7 and B20 retailed.
Oct 2025 - New oil plan: E20 and B7 become main fuels; GSH91/95 and E85 phased out by 2027; SAF 1% from 2026 rising to 8% by 2036.
Mar 2026 - Oil-crisis measures: diesel base blend B5 to B7 from 14 Mar 2026; E20 kept at least 5 baht per litre cheaper than E10; B20 sales resumed.
Biofuel subsidies extended two years to 24 Sep 2026.
thailand.latest: B7 diesel base (since 14 Mar 2026), E20 promoted over E10, SAF 1% in 2026.
thailand.pending: Possible later move to B10/B20; subsidy extension beyond 24 Sep 2026 not confirmed.
thailand.flags: Thai media call the SAF figure a mandate; a policy roundup lists it as a non-binding target.

philippines.name: Philippines
philippines.policy: Biofuels Act of 2006 (RA 9367): mandatory blending of locally sourced bioethanol and coco-biodiesel; the National Biofuels Board can recommend adjustments.
philippines.implemented: Act signed Jan 2007; B1 on effectivity, B2 in 2009, E10 in 2013.
changes: 2013 - Nationwide E10 mandate.
May 2024 - Energy Department circulars: B3 (from Oct 2024 per press), planned B4 (Oct 2025) and B5 (Oct 2026); voluntary E20 allowed.
2025 - B4/B5 steps suspended after international coconut oil prices rose over 300%.
Mar 2026 - Committee backed immediate B5; proposed law to suspend blending for up to a year during abnormal price movements and allow biofuel imports above a price threshold.
Jun 2026 - Agriculture Secretary backed immediate B5.
philippines.latest: E10 mandate plus voluntary E20 (only nine E20 stations); B3 in force; B5 not implemented (USDA, Jul 2026).
philippines.pending: Decision on B5; House Bill 4151 (amending the Biofuels Act); suspension / import bill.
philippines.flags: B3 start date taken from a May 2024 press headline.

vietnam.name: Vietnam
vietnam.policy: Roadmap for ethanol-blended gasoline (E5 moving to E10).
changes: Sep 2025 - Government decided to mandate E10 (reported as tied to US trade balance).
Nov 2025 - E10 start set for Jun 2026, six months later than first planned.
11 Feb 2026 - Ministry of Industry and Trade confirmed the switch to ethanol-blended gasoline in 2026.
1 Jun 2026 - E10 scheduled to become the only gasoline grade sold nationwide.
vietnam.latest: E10 nationwide from 1 Jun 2026 (as scheduled in Mar 2026 sources).

china.name: China
china.policy: E10 fuel ethanol policy (2017 plan) enforced unevenly at provincial level; no national biodiesel mandate.
china.implemented: Ethanol trial provinces from the 2000s†; 13 Sep 2017 national plan for nationwide E10 by 2020.
changes: 2017 - Plan to expand E10 from trial provinces to the whole country by 2020.
Late 2020 - State Council called for controlling ethanol processing capacity; E10 enforcement waned.
2022 - National average ethanol blend about 1.8%; biodiesel blend only 0.2-0.3%.
2024-26 - Producers pivoted from biodiesel exports to SAF after EU trade defense measures; SAF capacity about 3.3 Mt/yr; CAAC directives; trials 2026-2030.
china.latest: No new national ethanol mandate found; E10 remains the official goal; biodiesel receives no mandate (minor tax incentives); SAF deployment still limited.
china.pending: Industry expects a SAF mandate of about 5% by 2030 (not enacted); unofficial talk of an E5 mandate.
china.flags: Much of the evidence is USDA/IEA material through 2022 plus trade press - check the latest USDA China Biofuels Annual.

japan.name: Japan
japan.policy: Biofuel standard under the Sophisticated Methods Act (500 mn liters crude-oil equivalent per year, about 824 mn liters of ethanol, mostly via ETBE) plus a roadmap to E10 and E20.
changes: Nov 2024 - Government announced E10 by 2030 and E20 by 2040.
Feb 2025 - 7th Strategic Energy Plan includes a roadmap for nationwide E10 by FY2030.
10 Jun 2025 - METI action plan: small-scale E10 in Okinawa from FY2028; nationwide E10 option by 2030; biofuel GHG-reduction target 55% (to rise to 60% after a new gasoline life-cycle assessment).
2024-25 - Annual 824 mn liter target met; average blend 1.9% in 2025.
japan.latest: Annual target maintained to FY2028; voluntary E10 option planned alongside ETBE; SAF goal of 1.2 bn liters (about 10%) by 2030.
japan.pending: Nationwide E10 by FY2030; E20 by 2040.

south-korea.name: South Korea
south-korea.policy: Renewable Fuel Standard under the Renewable Energy Act: mandatory biodiesel blend in diesel.
south-korea.implemented: Voluntary blending from 2006; mandatory from 2012; legal RFS obligation 2013; 2.5% from 2015.
changes: Statutory ladder - 4.5% (2027-29) and 5.0% from 2030.
south-korea.pending: 4.5% from 2027 and 5% from 2030 (statute); SAF 1% for international flights from 2027 under consideration.
south-korea.flags: Trade press says the government plans 8% by 2030, which conflicts with the 5% statutory figure.

australia.name: Australia
australia.policy: No federal mandate; state mandates in New South Wales and Queensland.
australia.implemented: NSW ethanol mandate 2007†; Queensland biofuels mandate 2017†.
changes: Early 2025 - Federal review reportedly confirmed NSW E6/B2 and Queensland E4/B0.5 stay until a national low-carbon fuels framework (2027).
21 May 2026 - Government said it will introduce biofuel blending mandates and is expediting a public consultation to launch within months, citing energy security.
australia.latest: State mandates in force; a federal mandate is under development.
australia.pending: National mandate; industry urges a start before 2029.
australia.flags: Early-2025 review detail comes from an aggregator roundup.

south-africa.name: South Africa
south-africa.policy: Biofuels Regulatory Framework and mandatory blending regulations: minimum 2% bioethanol in petrol and 5% biodiesel in diesel from locally produced biofuels.
south-africa.implemented: Biofuels Industrial Strategy 2007; blending regulations gazetted 23 Aug 2012 (GN R.671), with effect from Oct 2015.
changes: 13 Dec 2019 - Cabinet approved the Regulatory Framework; gazetted 7 Feb 2020.
12 Mar 2021 - Draft amendment blending regulations published for comment.
2025 - Regulations gazetted / refined.
2026 - Industry says pricing (a base price) and VAT on sorghum remain hurdles.
south-africa.latest: Framework and regulations in place; effective implementation still constrained (May-Jun 2026 reporting). An aggregator roundup says implementation was targeted for Jan 2026.
south-africa.pending: Resolution of pricing and subsidy mechanism.
south-africa.flags: Whether the 2025 regulations are in operation is unclear in sources found.

other-africa-snapshot.name: Other Africa (snapshot)

United States of America.blendNote: No fixed national blend: the federal RFS sets annual volume obligations.

Canada.blendNote: Minimum renewable content in gasoline / diesel; provinces add higher or domestic-content rules (e.g. BC diesel 8%).

Brazil.blendNote: E30 / B15 since 1 Aug 2025. Temporary E32 approved 14 Jul 2026 (effective date unconfirmed).

Argentina.blendNote: Law 27,640, valid to 2030. Up to 15% ethanol allowed voluntarily since Mar 2026.

Paraguay.blendNote: Ethanol E30 since Mar 2025; May 2026 law conflicting reports. Biodiesel 7% to 31 Dec 2026.

Spain.note: National RED III transposition is still a draft; EU-level rules apply.

Netherlands.note: National RED III reform was still in draft in the latest source found (late 2025).

India.blendNote: E20 nationwide from 1 Apr 2026. Biodiesel: 5% target by 2030 (not in force).

Indonesia.blendNote: B50 from 1 Jul 2026 (three-month transition); B40 in Jan-Jun 2026. Ethanol: E3 allowance only.

Malaysia.blendNote: B15 in Peninsular Malaysia from 1 Jun 2026; B20 in some regions.

Thailand.blendNote: E10 base, E20 promoted; diesel base B7 from 14 Mar 2026 (B20 also sold).

Vietnam.blendNote: E10 as the only gasoline grade from 1 Jun 2026 (scheduled).

China.blendNote: E10 is the official goal; actual national average about 1.8% (2022). No biodiesel mandate.

Japan.blendNote: No fixed blend; volume standard (mostly ETBE). Target E10 by 2030, E20 by 2040.

Australia.blendNote: State mandates only: New South Wales E6/B2, Queensland E4/B0.5. No federal mandate yet.

South Africa.blendNote: Minimum levels in the blending regulations; implementation constrained.
